Author: Surya Kant
Bench: Surya Kant
1  IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA  CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL
APPEAL No.5243 OF 2024

(Arising out of SLP(Crl.)No.9350/2019)
 RANI SINGH   Versus  PAWAN   O R D E R  1.

Leave granted.
 2.

The appellant is aggrieved by the judgment dated 12.12.2018,
 passed by the High Court of Madhya Pradesh at Indore, whereby the  High Court, in an application filed by the appellant, seeking leave  to appeal against the judgment of acquittal dated  passed by the Judicial Magistrate First Class, 
 Pradesh, in Regular Criminal Trial No. 119/12, has declined to  interfere with the said judgment and consequently dism  said application.
 3.

sentences.text: It seems that the appellant and the respondent knew each other  from their student days.

Both were adults when the marriage is  claimed to have been performed between them on 02.03.2008 at Arya Rani Singh vs Pawan on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51686711/
1  Samaj Mandir, Bhagirathpura, Indore.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The respondent, thereafter,
 allegedly told the appellant on 10.07.2008 that he had got married Signature Not Verified Digitally signed by SATISH KUMAR YADAV Date: 2024.12.17 18:18:25 IST  to another woman, namely, Anjali @ Sonu and that he does not want Reason:
 to continue the relationship with the appellant any further.
This  2 led the appellant to lodge a complaint against the respondent vide Case Crime No.407/2008, dated 12.07.2008, under Sections 376 and 506 IPC, at P.S. Kotwali Dewas, M.P.
The trial took place in which the respondent was acquitted vide judgment dated 21.11.2017.

Th appellant, thereafter, moved an application under Section 378(4)
read with Section 482 Cr.P.C. and sought leave to appeal against the judgment of acquittal dated 21.11.2017, which has bee dismissed by the High Court, concluding as follows:
 5.

In view of the fact that the applicant herself  has not discharged the onus upon her of proving herself to  be legally wedded wife of Pawan, she cannot submit that  Pawan contracted second marriage during subsistence of  first marriage.

In the case in hand neither the applicant  has proved the performance of this ceremony in her  marriage with Pawan nor the second marriage with Anjali @
 Sonu with Pawan.
In view of the above, I see no reason to  interfere with the judgment of the trial Court dated  21.11.2017, therefore, leave to appeal against acquittal  cannot be granted.

4. We have heard learned counsel for the parties at  considerable length and carefully perused the material placed on Rani Singh vs Pawan on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51686711/
2 record.
5.

It is vehemently urged that the respondent, in hi statement as well as in the cross-examination by the appellant, has claimed that they were legally wedded husband and wife but later on he resiled from that statement.

The version of the respondent has been misconstrued by the courts in holding that the appellant failed to prove the performance of her marriage with the respondent or the alleged second marriage performed by the respondent with Anjali @ Sonu.

6. The aforesaid being a pure question of fact, we do not  3 find any ground to interfere with the impugned order except to clarify that the finding of the Trial Court/High Court that there existed no valid marriage between the parties, was only in the context of and for the purpose of deciding the criminal proceedings and nothing more.
The appellant may resort to the appropriate recourse, if so advised and in accordance with law.
7. The appeal is, accordingly, dismissed with liberty aforementioned.
8. As a result, the pending interlocutory applications also stand disposed of.
